newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes remain in slumber, outrights gain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes remain in slumber, outrights gain.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices gained slightly Wednesday morning on consolidative buying following Tuesday's widespread technical sell-off on the NYMEX market.
At the same time, the activity level on the domestic cash grade scene remained low. Traders eyed little in the way of fresh deals, noting refiner demand has not yet appeared for July barrels.
"It's thin and quiet, a lot of people aren't around this week," said a cash dealer in Houston.
July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing marked gains of around 5 cents to put benchmark at $20.80-90 a barrel. July/August rolls moved out a few pennies to 9-10 cents in favor of second month August.
The only confirmed grade number to switch hands was a parcel of West Texas Sour/Midland at -$1.53, steady from talk late on Tuesday.

Sour barrels were expected to find strength from word Iraq cancelled two cargoes of Basrah Light deliveries for 2.2 million barrels. Apparently, Baghdad fears the two contracts would push oil sales receipts over the $2.14 billion ceiling spelled-out in the U.N.-Iraq oil-for-food accord.
Traders said even if the oil accord is renewed at present levels by the Security Council next week, there would be a lag in signing new contracts, alleviating pressure on sours.
Other market talk saw Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James talked at WTI/Cushing minus 8-4 cents and Midland/WTI around 40-35 cents below benchmark.
